text.p: State-controlled Land Bank of the Philippines said on Friday it has foreclosed some properties of North Negros Marketing Corp in partial payments of its debts worth 465.62 million pesos.
North Negros is the trading arm of Philippine sugar miller Victorias Milling Corp.

The bank said it foreclosed on Wednesday six titles to 9,072 square meters of property at a subdivision in Bacolod City in central Philippines and two titles covering 4,388 square meters of land in another part of the city.
Both properties were mortgaged to the bank for 99 million pesos.
Land Bank said some 340.87 million of the outstanding loans of North Negros had been overdue since April this year.
The bank said it had offered North Negros options to pay its loans, including arranging the sale of some 100,000 bags of sugar.
"These bags of sugar in the form of refined sugar delivery orders (RSDOs) were used by North negros to secure its loans," it said.
"Subsequently, however, these RSDOs were declared unauthorised since there was no physical sugar to cover these orders," it added.
Land Bank said it decided to file a foreclosure case against North Negros after it established that the firm "was in no position to pay its loans."
Victorias had sought a debt moratorium on principal payment of its 4.423 billion loans from 32 local and foreign creditors due to the slump in the local sugar industry.
Creditors of Victorias have formed a committee to draw a restructuring programme for the sugar miller.
The news of the foreclosure of the properties of its trading arm did not affect Victorias shares.
Victorias shares jumped 18 centavos to two pesos in late trade at the Philippine Stock Exchange.
